Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On March 25, 2024, Ørsted announced it was selected by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations to begin negotiations for up to $100 million in federal funding. The funding is designated for the construction of a large-scale Power-to-X facility named Star e-Methanol, to be located along the Texas Gulf Coast. This project was one of 33 chosen to demonstrate commercial-scale decarbonization solutions. The facility is expected to produce up to 300,000 metric tons of e-methanol annually, which can be used as marine shipping fuel or as an input for sustainable aviation fuel and chemical production. The project will involve building new onshore wind and solar projects to power the creation of green hydrogen and will capture biogenic carbon from a local industrial facility to synthesize into e-methanol. <2> Methanex is a major methanol producer; Methanex reported its average realized price for methanol in the third quarter of 2023 was $303 per tonne; The average realized price in the third quarter of 2023 was a decrease from $338 per tonne in the second quarter of 2023 <3> US Methanol LLC's Liberty One plant began production in 2023; The Liberty One plant was in the process of ramping up to full capacity; The company announced on August 18, 2023, that it had repaid bonds on August 3, 2023 <4> The US Methanol 'Liberty One' plant, located in Institute, West Virginia, held its official opening ceremony on April 24, 2023, marking the completion of a project that involved relocating and rebuilding the facility from Brazil. [8, 9, 11] While the official opening celebration occurred in April 2023, production had commenced earlier, with some reports indicating an August 2022 start after construction completion that year. [9] The plant, a $250 million investment, has a production capacity of 200,000 metric tons of methanol per year. [8, 11] By the time of its official opening, the plant was already operating at approximately 95% capacity and shipping products to customers, contributing a new source of supply to the market. [9] This output served the market throughout the latter half of 2023, including the fourth quarter.

This project was one of 33 chosen to demonstrate commercial-scale decarbonization solutions. The facility is expected to produce up to 300,000 metric tons of e-methanol annually, which can be used as marine shipping fuel or as an input for sustainable aviation fuel and chemical production. The initial project is a commercial-scale demonstration at Montauk's Atascocita Humble Renewable Energy (HRE) facility in Humble, Texas. Leveraging Emvolon's patented technology, which repurposes car engines into modular chemical plants, the venture will convert flared gas that would otherwise be wasted into low-carbon methanol. The partners aim to develop a portfolio of sites with a combined annual production capacity of up to 50,000 metric tonnes of green methanol by 2030, targeting hard-to-decarbonize sectors such as chemical manufacturing, shipping, and aviation. <4> Methanex announced in the third quarter of 2024 its definitive agreement to acquire the international methanol business of OCI Global; The acquisition is for approximately $2.05 billion; The deal includes OCI's interests in two methanol facilities in Beaumont, Texas <5> In late June 2024, an analysis highlighted that North American methanol producers experienced strong margins in the first half of the year. [1] This was attributed to market tightness, partly resulting from production issues, which gave them some of the highest margins globally. [1] However, the analysis predicted a drop in North American methanol prices in the second half of 2024, which would lead to shrinking margins by the end of the year. [1] An earlier analysis from late May 2024 also forecasted margin challenges for the second half of the year due to global oversupply and concerns about the methanol market, though it suggested that North American producers' margins were unlikely to turn negative. [2] <6> On March 25, 2024, Ørsted announced it was selected by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations to begin negotiations for up to $100 million in federal funding. The funding is designated for the construction of a large-scale Power-to-X facility named Star e-Methanol, to be located along the Texas Gulf Coast. This project was one of 33 chosen to demonstrate commercial-scale decarbonization solutions. The facility is expected to produce up to 300,000 metric tons of e-methanol annually, which can be used as marine shipping fuel or as an input for sustainable aviation fuel and chemical production. The project will involve building new onshore wind and solar projects to power the creation of green hydrogen and will capture biogenic carbon from a local industrial facility to synthesize into e-methanol. <7> On February 20, 2024, Methanex Corporation announced that the start of commercial production at its new 1.8 million tonne Geismar 3 (G3) methanol plant in Louisiana was delayed. [2, 11] The delay was necessary due to significant damage to a large number of supporting refractory bricks in the autothermal reformer (ATR), which occurred during the final stages of the initial start-up process. [2, 3, 4] At the time of the announcement, the company believed the replacement of the specialty bricks could postpone the start of commercial production until the end of the third quarter of 2024. [2, 3] Later reports confirmed that the G3 plant produced its first methanol in July 2024 and, after a couple of shutdowns for equipment calibration, began operating at full rates in early October 2024. [7, 8, 9] <8> Methanex is a major methanol producer; Methanex reported its average realized price for methanol in the third quarter of 2023 was $303 per tonne; The average realized price in the third quarter of 2023 was a decrease from $338 per tonne in the second quarter of 2023 <9> US Methanol LLC's Liberty One plant began production in 2023; The Liberty One plant was in the process of ramping up to full capacity; The company announced on August 18, 2023, that it had repaid bonds on August 3, 2023 <10> The US Methanol 'Liberty One' plant, located in Institute, West Virginia, held its official opening ceremony on April 24, 2023, marking the completion of a project that involved relocating and rebuilding the facility from Brazil. [8, 9, 11] While the official opening celebration occurred in April 2023, production had commenced earlier, with some reports indicating an August 2022 start after construction completion that year. [9] The plant, a $250 million investment, has a production capacity of 200,000 metric tons of methanol per year. [8, 11] By the time of its official opening, the plant was already operating at approximately 95% capacity and shipping products to customers, contributing a new source of supply to the market. [9] This output served the market throughout the latter half of 2023, including the fourth quarter.

This significant growth in export demand, coupled with rising domestic consumption, is expected to put upward pressure on the price of natural gas, a key feedstock for methanol production. This situation was caused by several factors, including significant production curtailments at Methanex's Beaumont, Texas, facilities from June to September 2025, driven by volatility in the regional natural gas market. Compounding the issue were both planned and unplanned outages at other facilities. Notably, Methanex's Geismar 3 plant had an unplanned outage in the first quarter of 2025 with repairs extending into the second quarter, and the Natgasoline facility also faced supply disruptions from maintenance in early 2025, further tightening the market. <3> Throughout August 2025, Henry Hub natural gas prices, a primary feedstock for methanol, demonstrated significant volatility, with prices peaking at $3.05/MMBtu and dropping to a low of $2.78/MMBtu. The collaboration will combine Emvolon's technology, which converts methane-containing feed gas from sources like landfills and dairy farms into renewable methanol, with Freepoint's global market reach and logistics expertise. These companies were accused of engaging in transactions worth millions of dollars for Iranian-origin goods, with methanol being the most significantly affected product, alongside others like polyethylene and toluene. The action caused immediate and significant disruption in the Asian petrochemical market, as traders and buyers began to avoid Iranian cargoes. This led to a sharp increase in feedstock prices for downstream producers, with India's domestic methanol prices rising notably on July 31, 2025, amid concerns over supply interruptions and thinning profit margins. <9> An industry outlook for 2025 anticipates that methanol prices will remain moderately firm. The price was published on July 21, 2025, and is valid for the period of July 1, 2025, to September 30, 2025. [8] <10> A market forecast for the third quarter of 2025, published on July 19, 2025, indicates that the methanol market is anticipated to maintain relative stability. Pricing variations during this period are expected to be primarily driven by local supply and demand dynamics, as well as the costs of feedstock. Furthermore, a seasonal uptick in consumption for fuel applications could exert upward pressure on prices.

This decline was driven by aggressive year-end inventory clearance by producers and weak spot demand. Unlike the original RCV project that was to use biomass gasification, StormFisher will utilize clean hydrogen and captured CO2 to produce the methanol. This expansion is driven by new projects, including Plaquemines LNG and Corpus Christi LNG Stage 3, coming online. The EIA projects these additions will increase total U.S. LNG exports to an average of 16.3 Bcf/d in 2026, up from 11.9 Bcf/d in 2024. This significant growth in export demand, coupled with rising domestic consumption, is expected to put upward pressure on the price of natural gas, a key feedstock for methanol production. The EIA forecasts the Henry Hub natural gas spot price to average $3.90 per million British thermal units in 2026, a substantial increase from the 2024 average of $2.20.
